title: Tenant-side review test
framing: Each row is a question a San Francisco tenant lawyer or Rent Board counsellor would ask about a proposed increase. If every row passes, the increase is in the normal range and procedurally clean. A failure on any row is the kind of defect that leads to a Rent Board petition.
caveat: This is a self-check built from the cited authorities. It is not legal advice and it is not a substitute for advice from a lawyer or a Rent Board counsellor.

tests.question: Is the percentage at or below the allowable annual increase plus properly banked amounts?
tests.pass_condition: Total percentage equals the annual rate in force on the effective date, plus only those skipped years that satisfy the 24-month banking test.
tests.unit2: Yes at 13.1%, provided the increase is effective on or before February 28, 2027 and no increase has been taken since June 1, 2019.

tests.question: Was the calculation done by adding percentages, not compounding?
tests.pass_condition: Percentages summed, then applied once to the current base rent.

tests.question: Was the increase applied to base rent only, with no passthrough folded in?
tests.pass_condition: Base rent plus housing services such as parking or storage; excludes temporary passthroughs and fluctuating charges.
tests.unit1: Base rent $3,995 assumed to be all base rent. Not verified - see FLAG-06.
tests.unit2: Base rent $3,150 assumed to be all base rent. Not verified - see FLAG-06.

tests.question: Was the amount rounded up?
tests.pass_condition: No rounding up to the nearest dollar.
tests.unit1: $63.92 and $119.85 are exact to the cent; nothing was rounded up.
tests.unit2: $412.65 is exact to the cent; nothing was rounded up.

tests.question: Is it at least 12 months since the last increase (or since the lease began)?
tests.unit1: Yes for a February 1, 2027 effective date, which is 24 months after the February 1, 2025 lease start.
tests.unit2: Yes. First increase proposed after a June 1, 2019 lease start.

tests.question: Is the notice period long enough for the size of the increase?
tests.pass_condition: 30 days if 10% or less; 90 days if more than 10%; plus 5 days if served by mail.
tests.unit2: 90 days (95 if mailed). A 30-day notice at 13.1% fails this test.

tests.question: Does the notice state every required element?
tests.pass_condition: Dollar amount, percentage, effective date, which portion is annual and which is banked, served in the manner the statute allows.
tests.unit2: Achievable, and the banked portion must be itemised because Sec. 37.3(b)(1) requires it.

tests.question: Does the owner hold a current rent increase licence?
tests.pass_condition: Licence in effect on the effective date of the increase.
tests.unit1: Must be confirmed. Unverified - see FLAG-09.
tests.unit2: Must be confirmed. Unverified - see FLAG-09.

tests.question: Is the increase unconnected to any repair complaint, inspection or tenant organising?
tests.pass_condition: No tenantability complaint, citation, inspection or organising activity in the preceding 180 days.
tests.unit1: Must be confirmed. Unverified - see FLAG-10.
tests.unit2: Must be confirmed. Unverified - see FLAG-10.

tests.question: Is the increase unrelated to any protected characteristic?
tests.pass_condition: The basis for the amount is the published percentage and the tenancy's own history, applied under a written policy.
tests.unit1: Yes if applied under a written policy.
tests.unit2: Yes if applied under a written policy.

tests.question: Is the increase unrelated to any attempt to regain possession or to induce the tenant to leave?
tests.pass_condition: No eviction notice, buyout discussion or offer to vacate in the recent past, and no aim of re-renting at market.
tests.unit1: Must be confirmed. Unverified - see FLAG-10.
tests.unit2: Must be confirmed. Unverified - see FLAG-10.

tests.question: Was the amount set by hand rather than by a pricing tool?
tests.pass_condition: No algorithmic device using non-public competitor data was used.
tests.unit1: Must be confirmed. Unverified - see FLAG-10.
tests.unit2: Must be confirmed. Unverified - see FLAG-10.

tests.question: Is the increase justified by market rent or by how long the tenant has stayed?
tests.pass_condition: Neither is a lawful basis for exceeding the cap. A below-market long tenancy is expressly not an extraordinary circumstance.
tests.unit1: Not applicable - no such basis is proposed.
tests.unit2: The 13.1% is not justified on market grounds. It is justified only by the banked percentages. If the banked test fails, the ceiling drops to the annual rate.

tests.question: Can the tenant check the maths against the Rent Board's own table in under a minute?
tests.pass_condition: Yes, if the notice itemises each year's percentage.
tests.unit2: Yes if itemised; no if a single 13.1% figure is presented without the year-by-year breakdown.

verdict_template.unit1: Passes on the cited authorities for the items that can be assessed from the facts given. The open items are the licence, the absence of a recent complaint, and whether $3,995 is entirely base rent.
verdict_template.unit2: Passes on the cited authorities at 13.1% only if four conditions hold: no increase since June 1, 2019; effective on or before February 28, 2027; 90 days' notice; a current rent increase licence. Any one of those failing makes the increase defective or void.

if_a_tenant_petitions: The tenant can file a Tenant Petition (Form 516C) free of charge, with no time limit (S20).
If the notice is clearly unlawful on its face and has not yet taken effect, the tenant can file a Tenant Summary Petition (Form 518) (S22).
A tenant who received the notice within the last 60 days and whose landlord has not made required repairs can file Form 516B (S22).
The hearing is before a Rent Board Administrative Law Judge and is designed so that no one needs an attorney (S20).
The Rent Board does not adjudicate harassment, discrimination or retaliation; those go to court or another forum (S21).
